examples.en: My younger sibling goes in and out of the library all the time these days.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 우리 집에 뻔질나게 찾아와요.
examples.en: That person keeps turning up at our house.

examples.ko: 어릴 때는 친구와 놀이터를 뻔질나게 다녔어요.
examples.en: When we were kids, my friend and I went to the playground all the time.

examples.ko: 왜 그 가게에 그렇게 뻔질나게 가요?
examples.en: Why do you go to that shop so often?
The friend who used to contact me constantly has gone quiet lately.

examples.ko: 아버지는 출장 때문에 공항을 뻔질나게 오가세요.
examples.en: My father goes back and forth to the airport all the time because of business trips.

explain: '자주'보다 말맛이 강해서, 어떤 곳을 쉴 새 없이 드나드는 모습에 써요. 보통 '뻔질나게' 꼴로 '드나들다, 다니다, 찾아오다' 같은 말과 함께 나와요.
explain_en: It has a stronger flavor than '자주' (often) and describes going somewhere again and again without a break. It usually appears as '뻔질나게' together with verbs like '드나들다', '다니다' and '찾아오다'.

en: resist; hold out; hold fast to

examples.en: The child digs in and says he won't go to the hospital.
Don't hold out to the end, just apologize.

examples.ko: 동생이 숙제를 안 하겠다고 한참 뻗댔어요.
examples.en: My younger brother stubbornly refused to do his homework for a while.
If you dig in like that, nobody will help you.

examples.ko: 강아지가 산책이 싫어서 현관에서 뻗대고 있어요.
examples.en: The puppy doesn't want a walk and is planting its feet at the front door.

examples.ko: 그렇게 뻗대던 친구도 결국 와 줬어요.
examples.en: Even the friend who had been so stubborn finally came.

explain: '버티다'와 비슷하지만 '뻗대다'는 남의 말을 듣지 않고 고집스럽게 맞서는 느낌이 강해요. 대체로 좋지 않은 뜻으로 쓰고, 아이나 가까운 사람의 고집을 말할 때 많이 나와요.
explain_en: It is similar to '버티다' (to hold out), but '뻗대다' strongly suggests stubbornly refusing to listen and pushing back. It is mostly negative and often used for children or people close to you being obstinate.

examples.en: My fingers went stiff from the cold.
I sat too stiffly in the interview.

examples.ko: 아이가 사진을 찍을 때 뻣뻣이 서 있어요.
examples.en: The child stands stiffly when having a photo taken.

examples.ko: 풀을 먹인 셔츠가 뻣뻣이 서 있어요.
examples.en: The starched shirt stands up stiffly.
He walked past with his head held stiffly high.
I was so nervous on stage that my body froze up stiffly.

explain: 형용사 '뻣뻣하다'의 짝이에요. 몸이나 물건이 굳어서 잘 안 구부러질 때도 쓰고, 고개를 숙이지 않는 거만한 태도를 말할 때도 써요. 말할 때는 '뻣뻣하게'도 자주 써요.
explain_en: It is the adverb partner of the adjective '뻣뻣하다'. It describes a body or object that is stiff and does not bend, and also a proud attitude of not bowing one's head. In speech '뻣뻣하게' is also common.

examples.en: The snow squeaked when I stepped on it.
I scrubbed the plate until it squeaked, and now it sparkles.

examples.ko: 깨끗이 씻은 그릇에서 뽀드득 소리가 나요.
examples.en: The well-washed bowl makes a squeaky sound.
The kids walk along crunching through the snow.

examples.ko: 체육관 바닥에서 운동화가 뽀드득 소리를 내요.
examples.en: Sneakers squeak on the gym floor.

examples.ko: 겨울 아침에 뽀드득 눈 밟는 소리가 좋아요.
examples.en: I like the crunch of stepping on snow on a winter morning.

explain: 쌓인 눈을 밟을 때나 깨끗이 씻은 물건을 문지를 때 나는 소리예요. 소리가 반복되면 '뽀드득뽀드득'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It is the sound of stepping on packed snow or rubbing something that has been washed clean. When the sound repeats, you say '뽀드득뽀드득'.

examples.en: My father often listens to trot music in the car.
My friend sang old trot songs with gusto at karaoke.
Do young people these days like trot too?
Trot music is blaring out of the market.

examples.ko: 할머니가 뽕짝 리듬에 맞춰 어깨를 흔드셨어요.
examples.en: Grandma swayed her shoulders to the trot rhythm.

examples.ko: 이 노래는 뽕짝 느낌이 나서 정겨워요.
examples.en: This song has a trot feel, so it feels warm and familiar.

explain: 트로트를 편하게, 조금 옛날식으로 부르는 말이에요. 말투에 따라 가볍게 보는 느낌이 있을 수 있어서, 격식 있는 자리에서는 '트로트'라고 해요.
explain_en: It is a casual, slightly old-fashioned way to say '트로트' (trot). Depending on tone it can sound a bit dismissive, so in formal settings people say '트로트'.

examples.en: My younger brother is sulking because he couldn't have a snack.
Why have you been sulking like that since morning?

examples.ko: 친구가 뾰로통한 얼굴로 아무 말도 안 했어요.
examples.en: My friend said nothing, with a sulky look on her face.

examples.ko: 장난감을 뺏기자 아이 표정이 금세 뾰로통해졌어요.
examples.en: When his toy was taken, the child's face quickly turned sulky.
My girlfriend sits there sulking and just looks out the window.
Even when she pouts she's so cute that I can't get angry.

explain: 화가 크게 난 것보다는 못마땅해서 말없이 입을 내밀고 있는 느낌이에요. 어린아이나 가까운 사람이 삐쳤을 때 많이 써요. '뽀로통하다'라고도 해요.
explain_en: It describes being displeased and silently pouting rather than being truly furious. It is often used for children or close people who are in a huff. '뽀로통하다' is also used for the same meaning.

examples.ko: 낡은 문을 열자 삐거덕 소리가 났어요.
examples.en: When I opened the old door, it creaked.

examples.ko: 계단을 올라갈 때마다 삐거덕 소리가 나요.
examples.en: The stairs creak every time I go up.
The chair creaked and then broke.

examples.ko: 침대가 삐거덕 소리를 내서 잠을 설쳤어요.
examples.en: The bed creaked, so I slept badly.
The front gate creaked open and Grandma came out.

examples.ko: 밤에 마루가 삐거덕 하는 소리에 깜짝 놀랐어요.
examples.en: I was startled at night by the sound of the floor creaking.

explain: 문, 마루, 의자처럼 나무나 쇠가 서로 눌리거나 비벼질 때 나는 소리예요. '삐걱'도 비슷한 소리를 나타내요.
explain_en: It is the sound made when wood or metal parts press or rub against each other, as with doors, wooden floors and chairs. '삐걱' describes a similar sound.

examples.en: The door creaks in the wind.
The old chair creaked every time I sat down.
The floor creaked, so I walked carefully.
The sound of the bed creaking woke me up.
The stairs creak, so please come down slowly.
The old bicycle creaked as it went up the hill.

explain: 문이나 마루, 의자 같은 것이 소리를 반복해서 내는 모습이에요. 소리가 한 번 날 때는 '삐거덕 소리가 나다'라고 해요. 같은 뜻으로 '삐걱거리다'도 써요.
explain_en: It describes things like doors, floors and chairs making that creaking sound repeatedly. For a single creak you say '삐거덕 소리가 나다'. '삐걱거리다' is also used with the same meaning.

examples.en: The plan went rocky from the start, so I was worried.
I can hear the old door creaking.
The teamwork is shaky.
The bed creaked all night.

examples.ko: 마루가 삐걱댈 때마다 할아버지 생각이 나요.
examples.en: Every time the floor creaks, I think of my grandfather.

examples.ko: 일이 삐걱대도 포기하지 말고 다시 해 봐요.
examples.en: Even if things go rocky, don't give up and try again.

explain: 문이나 마루가 내는 소리에도 쓰고, 일이나 사이가 순조롭지 않을 때 비유로도 많이 써요. 같은 뜻으로 '삐걱거리다'도 써요.

phrases.example: 결혼 후 부부 사이가 삐걱대기 시작했어요.
phrases.nuance_ko: 두 사람이나 조직의 관계가 순조롭지 않고 서로 맞지 않는 상태를 소리에 빗대어 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: It compares a strained relationship between people or within a group to a creaking sound, meaning things are not running smoothly.

explain_en: It is used for the sound of doors or floors, and also figuratively when work or a relationship is not going smoothly. '삐걱거리다' is also used with the same meaning.

examples.en: I twisted my ankle going down the stairs.
I tweaked my back and rested for a few days.
The moment I slipped, I almost fell.
I strained my shoulder lifting a heavy bag.

examples.ko: 발을 삐끗 디뎠는데 다행히 안 다쳤어요.
examples.en: My foot slipped as I stepped, but luckily I wasn't hurt.

examples.ko: 한 번 삐끗하면 계획 전체가 어긋나요.
examples.en: If you slip up once, the whole plan goes off track.

explain: 부사지만 보통 '삐끗하다' 꼴로 써요. 발목이나 허리의 관절이 갑자기 접질릴 때 쓰고, 일이 한 번 어긋나는 것에도 비유해서 써요.
explain_en: Though listed as an adverb, it is usually used as '삐끗하다'. It describes a joint such as an ankle or the back suddenly twisting, and is also used figuratively when something goes wrong once.

examples.en: The chicks are peeping in the yard.
The chick was cheeping from morning, so I woke up early.
The baby bird waits for its mother, cheeping.
The sound of chicks peeping is so cute.
The chicks in the box peeped all night.
The kids follow me chirping like chicks.

explain: 병아리나 아주 어린 새가 가늘고 짧게 우는 소리예요. 아이들이 귀엽게 재잘거릴 때 비유로 쓰기도 해요.
explain_en: It is the thin, short cry of chicks or very young birds. It is sometimes used figuratively when children chatter in a cute way.

examples.ko: 가방 밖으로 우산이 삐죽 나와 있어요.
examples.en: An umbrella is sticking out of the bag.

examples.ko: 담 너머로 아이 머리가 삐죽 보였어요.
examples.en: A child's head popped up over the wall.
I stepped carefully on the rocks jutting up everywhere.
A nail is sticking out, so be careful.
The child poked his face out through the gap in the door.
My toes are poking out of my sock.

explain: 무언가가 끝이 뾰족하게 밖으로 조금 나온 모습이에요. 여러 개가 여기저기 솟아 있으면 '삐죽삐죽'이라고 해요. 입을 내미는 동작은 '삐죽거리다'로 말해요.
explain_en: It describes something with a pointed tip sticking out a little. When many things stick up here and there, you say '삐죽삐죽'. Pushing out the lips is expressed with '삐죽거리다'.

examples.en: The child is holding back tears, pushing out his lips.

examples.ko: 기분이 상했는지 동생이 계속 입을 삐죽거려요.
examples.en: My younger sibling keeps pouting, probably upset.
Don't pout, say it in words.
It was cute to see my friend pouting.
She pouted because she didn't get praised.

examples.ko: 그 아이는 서운하면 삐죽거려서 금방 알 수 있어요.
examples.en: When that child feels hurt she pouts, so it's easy to tell.

explain: 서운하거나 울음이 날 때 입술을 내미는 동작이에요. '입을 삐죽거리다'처럼 자주 쓰고, 같은 뜻으로 '삐죽이다'나 '삐죽대다'도 있어요.
explain_en: It is the movement of pushing out the lips when feeling hurt or about to cry, often as '입을 삐죽거리다'. '삐죽이다' and '삐죽대다' also exist with the same meaning.

en: sweating bit by bit; beading (of sweat)

examples.en: It's hot, so sweat keeps beading on my forehead.

examples.ko: 발표 전에 긴장해서 삐질삐질 땀을 흘렸어요.
examples.en: I was nervous before the presentation and broke out in a sweat.
When the teacher called me, I broke into a cold sweat.

examples.ko: 에어컨이 고장 나서 삐질삐질 땀을 흘리며 일했어요.
examples.en: The air conditioner broke, so I worked sweating away.

examples.ko: 거짓말이 들킬까 봐 삐질삐질 땀이 나더라고요.
examples.en: I was afraid my lie would be found out, and I started sweating.

examples.ko: 매운 음식을 먹었더니 삐질삐질 땀이 나요.
examples.en: I ate spicy food and now I'm sweating.

explain: 땀이 조금씩 계속 배어 나오는 모습이에요. 더울 때뿐 아니라 긴장하거나 당황했을 때도 많이 써요. 땀을 아주 많이 흘릴 때는 '뻘뻘'을 써요.
explain_en: It describes sweat seeping out bit by bit. It is used not only when hot but also when nervous or flustered. For heavy sweating, '뻘뻘' is used instead.

examples.en: When I blew the whistle, it let out a shrill sound.
When I tapped the card, it beeped.

examples.ko: 마이크에서 삑 하는 소리가 나서 놀랐어요.
examples.en: The microphone squealed and startled me.
The microwave beeps when it's done.

examples.ko: 노래 부르다가 고음에서 삑 소리가 났어요.
examples.en: My voice cracked on the high note while singing.
I heard a beep as the door locked.

explain: 호루라기나 기계에서 나는 짧고 높은 소리예요. 소리가 이어지면 '삑삑'이라고 해요. 노래할 때 음이 틀어지는 것을 '삑사리가 나다'라고도 해요.
explain_en: It is a short, high sound from a whistle or a machine. When the sound repeats, you say '삑삑'. In singing, a cracked note is also called '삑사리가 나다'.

examples.en: The alarm beeped and woke me up.

examples.ko: 후진할 때 차에서 삑삑 소리가 나요.
examples.en: The car beeps when it reverses.
The traffic light changed with a beeping sound.
The machine is beeping to say the battery is low.
I called the children, blowing the whistle again and again.

examples.ko: 문을 열어 두었더니 경고음이 삑삑 났어요.
examples.en: I left the door open and the warning alarm started beeping.

explain: '삑'이 반복되는 소리로, 알람이나 경고음, 호루라기에 많이 써요. 계속 나면 '삑삑거리다'라고 해요.
explain_en: It is the repeated version of '삑', commonly used for alarms, warning sounds and whistles. When it goes on continuously, you say '삑삑거리다'.

examples.en: The scale turned on with a beeping sound.
The fridge door is open, so it's beeping.
The alarm kept beeping from morning, so it was noisy.
The machine keeps beeping. What's wrong?
The toy whistle keeps squeaking, and the child loves it.

examples.ko: 화재 경보기가 삑삑거려서 모두 밖으로 나갔어요.
examples.en: The fire alarm started beeping, so everyone went outside.

explain: 알람이나 경고음, 호루라기 같은 기계 소리에 주로 써요. 한 번 나면 '삑 소리가 나다'라고 하고, 사람이 높고 날카롭게 소리를 지르면 '빽빽거리다'를 써요.
explain_en: It is mainly used for machine sounds such as alarms, warning beeps and whistles. A single sound is '삑 소리가 나다', and when a person yells in a high, sharp voice, '빽빽거리다' is used.

examples.en: My friends sat in a circle around the table.
I went all the way around the park and broke a sweat.
The kids gathered in a ring around the teacher.

examples.ko: 집 주변에 나무를 삥 둘러 심었어요.
examples.en: We planted trees in a ring around the house.

examples.ko: 갑자기 어지러워서 방이 삥 도는 것 같았어요.
examples.en: I suddenly felt dizzy, as if the room were spinning.

examples.ko: 길을 몰라서 같은 동네를 삥 돌아서 왔어요.
examples.en: I didn't know the way, so I came around the same neighborhood in a loop.

explain: 둥글게 한 바퀴 도는 모양이나 빙 둘러서 있는 모양에 써요. '빙'보다 조금 센 느낌이 있어요. 어지러울 때는 '핑 돌다'를 더 흔히 써요.
explain_en: It describes going once around in a circle or standing in a ring. It feels slightly stronger than '빙'. For dizziness, '핑 돌다' is more common.

examples.en: The pencil scratches softly on the paper.

examples.ko: 사과를 베어 물자 사각거리는 소리가 났어요.
examples.en: When I bit into the apple, it made a crisp crunching sound.
The fallen leaves rustle under my feet, which feels nice.
In the library, I could only hear the sound of writing scratching.
The new blanket rustles softly and feels nice.
The ice crunched every time I chewed it.

explain: 연필로 쓸 때, 과일이나 얼음을 씹을 때처럼 얇고 단단한 것이 스치거나 부서지며 나는 가벼운 소리예요. 반복형 '사각사각'도 자주 써요.
explain_en: It is the light sound of thin, firm things rubbing or breaking, such as writing with a pencil or chewing fruit or ice. The repeated form '사각사각' is also used often.

en: being on the brink of death; deadly situation; being near death

examples.en: He hovered between life and death after a traffic accident.

examples.ko: 환자가 사경에 놓여서 가족들이 병원을 지켰어요.
examples.en: The patient was in critical condition, so the family stayed at the hospital.
The patient who came back from the brink recognized his family.
Grandfather, who had been near death, fortunately woke up.
I got lost in the mountains and was in mortal danger.

examples.ko: 큰 수술을 받고도 한동안 사경을 넘나들었어요.
examples.en: Even after major surgery, he went back and forth near death for a while.

explain: 죽을 고비를 말하고, 보통 '사경을 헤매다'처럼 정해진 꼴로 나와요. 뉴스나 글에서 자주 보이고, 일상 대화에서는 '죽을 뻔했어요'라고 해요.

phrases.example: 그는 큰 사고를 당하고 며칠 동안 사경을 헤맸어요.
phrases.nuance_ko: 목숨이 위태로워서 살지 죽을지 알 수 없는 상태가 이어지는 모습이에요. 뉴스나 글에서 많이 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: It describes a stretch of time when someone's life is in danger and could go either way. It appears often in news and writing.

explain_en: It refers to a life-or-death crisis and usually appears in the fixed form '사경을 헤매다'. You see it in news and writing, while in everyday talk people say '죽을 뻔했어요' (I almost died).

examples.en: The cadets are marching on the field.

examples.ko: 삼촌은 공군 사관생도가 되려고 열심히 공부해요.
examples.en: My uncle studies hard to become an air force cadet.
Cadets live under strict rules.
At the graduation ceremony, the cadets saluted.

examples.ko: 형은 사관생도처럼 허리를 곧게 펴고 걸어요.
examples.en: My older brother walks with a straight back like a cadet.

examples.ko: 사관생도로 입학하려면 체력 시험도 봐야 해요.
examples.en: To enter as a cadet, you also have to take a fitness test.

explain: 장교가 되려고 사관학교에서 공부하고 훈련받는 학생이에요. 줄여서 '생도'라고도 하고, 학교는 '사관학교'라고 해요.
explain_en: It means a student who studies and trains at a military academy to become an officer. It can be shortened to '생도', and the school is called '사관학교'.

en: high society; beau monde; social circles

examples.ko: 그녀는 젊은 나이에 사교계의 스타가 됐어요.
examples.en: She became a star of high society at a young age.

examples.ko: 소설 속 주인공이 사교계에 처음 나가는 장면이에요.
examples.en: It's the scene where the novel's heroine first enters high society.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 사교계에서 이름이 알려져 있어요.
examples.en: That person is well known in society circles.

examples.ko: 옛날 유럽의 사교계 이야기를 영화로 봤어요.
examples.en: I watched a movie about old European high society.
I think high society is glamorous only on the surface.

examples.ko: 그는 사교계를 떠나 조용히 살기로 했어요.
examples.en: He decided to leave high society and live quietly.

explain: 상류층 사람들이 모여 어울리는 사회를 말하고, 소설이나 영화, 역사 이야기에서 많이 나와요. 요즘 일상에서는 '인맥이 넓다'처럼 다른 말로 표현해요.
explain_en: It refers to the world where upper-class people mix and socialize, and it appears often in novels, films and history stories. In daily talk today people use other expressions such as '인맥이 넓다' (to have wide connections).

en: the Four Gentlemen (plum blossom, orchid, chrysanthemum, bamboo)

examples.en: We learned to paint the Four Gentlemen in art class.
Grandfather enjoys painting the Four Gentlemen with a brush.
The Four Gentlemen are painted on this folding screen.

examples.ko: 사군자 중에서 난초를 그리는 게 제일 어려웠어요.
examples.en: Of the Four Gentlemen, painting the orchid was the hardest.
I looked at Four Gentlemen paintings at the museum.

examples.ko: 사군자 전시회에 가서 대나무 그림에 감탄했어요.
examples.en: I went to a Four Gentlemen exhibition and admired the bamboo painting.

explain: 매화, 난초, 국화, 대나무 네 가지를 함께 부르는 말로, 동양화에서 즐겨 그리는 소재예요. 곧은 선비의 마음을 상징한다고 해서 '군자'라는 이름이 붙었어요. 미술이나 서예 이야기에서 자주 들을 수 있어요.
explain_en: It is the collective name for plum blossom, orchid, chrysanthemum and bamboo, favorite subjects in East Asian painting. They are said to symbolize the upright character of a scholar, which is why they are called '군자'. You often hear it in talk about art and calligraphy.

examples.en: The flames are slowly dying down.
I'll wait a bit until my anger dies down.

examples.ko: 인기가 사그라들어서 요즘은 그 노래를 안 들어요.
examples.en: Its popularity faded, so I don't listen to that song these days.
As night came, the fever went down.
I can feel my initial passion fading.

examples.ko: 논란이 사그라들자 가게에 손님이 다시 왔어요.
examples.en: Once the controversy subsided, customers came back to the shop.

explain: 불, 열, 화, 인기처럼 센 것이 서서히 약해질 때 써요. '식다'와 비슷하지만 점점 잦아드는 느낌이 더 강해요. '사그라지다'도 같은 뜻이고, 'ㄹ'이 빠져서 '사그라드는, 사그라듭니다'가 돼요.
explain_en: It is used when something strong, such as fire, fever, anger or popularity, gradually weakens. It is similar to '식다' (to cool down) but feels more like slowly subsiding. '사그라지다' has the same meaning, and the ㄹ drops in forms like '사그라드는' and '사그라듭니다'.

examples.ko: 새로 온 직원이 사근사근해서 인기가 많아요.
examples.en: The new employee is so friendly that she's very popular.
My older sister has a gentle, kind personality.
She answered the phone in a warm, gentle voice.
Thank you for treating my child so kindly.
I still remember the amiable shop clerk.
Everyone praised the clerk for being so affable.

explain: 말씨와 태도가 부드럽고 상냥해서 가까이하기 편한 사람에게 써요. 반대로 퉁명스러운 사람은 '퉁명스럽다'고 해요. '싹싹하다'와 비슷하지만, '싹싹하다'는 붙임성 있고 눈치 빠른 느낌이 더 있어요.
explain_en: It is used for someone whose speech and manner are soft and kind, making them easy to approach. The opposite is '퉁명스럽다' (curt, blunt). It is similar to '싹싹하다', but '싹싹하다' adds a feeling of being sociable and quick to read situations.
